title: Choose a representation that survives production
description: Compare transformations against model geometry, holdout signal, dimensionality, stability, and online cost. The most elaborate option is not automatically the strongest feature.

scenarios.label: Skewed transaction amount
scenarios.prompt: Predict payment risk with a linear classifier. Most purchases are small, but a few are extremely large.
scenarios.constraint: Linear model, sub-5 ms feature budget

candidates.label: Keep raw amount
candidates.detail: Pass the dollar value directly to the model.
candidates.explanation: The feature is cheap, but a few very large values can dominate a linear decision boundary.
candidates.tradeoff: Reasonable for a tree baseline; less suitable for this linear geometry without another treatment.

candidates.label: Compress with log1p
candidates.detail: Preserve order while reducing the influence of a long positive tail.
candidates.risk: Requires a policy for negative or invalid values
candidates.explanation: The compressed geometry exposes relative differences without allowing a handful of large purchases to set the whole scale.
candidates.tradeoff: The transformed coefficient is less direct to explain in dollars, so retain the raw value for diagnostics.

candidates.label: Amount-to-income ratio
candidates.detail: Express purchase size relative to verified monthly income.
candidates.risk: Income may be stale, missing, or policy-sensitive
candidates.explanation: The ratio has strong business meaning, but its denominator introduces a new data dependency and missing-value path.
candidates.tradeoff: Ship only after defining income freshness, zero handling, access policy, and a fallback.

scenarios.label: High-cardinality merchant
scenarios.prompt: Represent 480 merchant categories for a churn model while handling new merchants at serving time.
scenarios.constraint: Frequent unknown values, modest training set

candidates.label: Map names to integers
candidates.detail: Assign each merchant category an arbitrary integer.
candidates.risk: Invents order and distance that do not exist
candidates.explanation: A linear model interprets nearby integers as nearby categories even though the assigned order is arbitrary.
candidates.tradeoff: Native categorical support in a different model family would be a separate design decision.

candidates.label: One-hot categories
candidates.detail: Create one indicator per known category and ignore unknown values.
candidates.risk: Rare and unseen categories create sparse, weak evidence
candidates.explanation: The representation does not invent order, but it creates a wide sparse feature space with limited evidence for rare merchants.
candidates.tradeoff: Group rare categories and measure whether the extra dimensions improve protected holdout slices.

candidates.label: Encode training frequency
candidates.detail: Replace each category with its frequency learned from the training partition.
candidates.risk: Frequency can drift and is not category identity
candidates.explanation: The compact value handles width and unknowns well, provided the mapping is learned from training data and versioned.
candidates.tradeoff: Monitor frequency drift and use an explicit fallback for categories absent from the fitted vocabulary.

scenarios.label: Hour-of-day cycle
scenarios.prompt: Represent request hour for a demand model where 23:00 and 00:00 should be close rather than far apart.

candidates.label: Keep hour 0-23
candidates.detail: Pass the clock hour as one integer.
candidates.explanation: The model sees 23 and 0 as far apart even though they are neighboring times on a clock.
candidates.tradeoff: A tree can split hour ranges, but it still needs several boundaries to approximate a smooth cycle.

candidates.label: One-hot 24 hours
candidates.detail: Give each hour an independent coefficient.
candidates.risk: Adjacent hours do not share statistical strength
candidates.explanation: One-hot encoding avoids false order but cannot express smooth adjacency without enough examples for each hour.
candidates.tradeoff: Use it when hour-specific discontinuities are real and the data supports 24 independent effects.

candidates.label: Encode sine and cosine
candidates.detail: Map the hour onto two coordinates on the unit circle.
candidates.explanation: The two coordinates preserve the wraparound at midnight and let a linear model learn a smooth daily cycle.
candidates.tradeoff: Add calendar or region context when the periodic pattern changes across populations.
